filter_schema.description:
List selection for the Invocation view — the typed, schema'd
filter (never a query language).
filter_schema.title: InvocationListFilter

index_schema.description:
One row in the invocation list: a coordination-ownership row, or (in
the merged index) an archive-only row flagged `archived`.

agent_id.description: From the projection; `None` when no event for the id has landed.

archived.description:
True when the row came from `invocation_archive` (no live
ownership row remains).

assigned_at_ms.description:
`assigned_at` for ownership rows; `archived_at` for archive-only
rows.

started_at_ms.description:
When the invocation began: `assigned_at` (dispatch time — the
closest thing to a start the coordination store records) for
ownership rows, the archive's true `started_at` for archive-only
rows. Unlike `assigned_at_ms`, this means the same thing on both
row kinds — the list surface's "started" column.

status.description:
`in_flight` / `completed` / `failed` / `ambiguous`, or the
archive's `final_phase` for archive-only rows.

worker_id.description: Empty for archive-only rows (the archive keeps no worker).

index_schema.title: InvocationSummaryView

key_schema.description: Get identity for the Invocation view.
key_schema.title: InvocationViewKey

EventView.description: One event row from the projection.

InvocationCostView.description: One invocation's share of an agent's spend.

started_at_ms.description:
Epoch ms of the invocation's first cost event (its effective
start as the projection sees it); 0 when the stored timestamp
fails to parse.

LiveExecutionView.description:
Live execution state of an in-flight invocation, from the worker WAL —
the "what is it doing right now" view. Present only while the invocation
has a WAL row (deleted on archive hand-off).

liveness.description: The health page's verdict for this run (see [`Liveness`]).

step_index.description:
Reducer *step* counter (every model and tool step) — not the
model-turn count that `max_iterations` gates (issue #109).

Liveness.description:
The per-invocation liveness verdict the health page counts —
shared by every surface that shows an in-flight row, so the health
tile, the active table, and the detail page cannot drift apart.

oneOf.description:
A fresh open dispatch (tool or LLM) — long runs are fine as
long as the dispatch itself is younger than the long-dispatch
threshold (#130).

Nothing open, but the WAL row advanced recently: the reducer is
between steps. The quiet, healthy in-between.

No fresh dispatch AND the WAL row has not advanced within the
stuck threshold — the row the operator needs to look at.

state_schema.description: Everything known about one invocation, composed across the three stores.

archive.description: Archive record, if the invocation has finalised.

cost.description:
The invocation's cost so far — llm calls, tokens, and spend
summed from the projection's cost-bearing events. Grows while
the run is live; `None` before the first priced call lands.

has_transcript.description: Whether the worker WAL contains dispatch rows for a transcript.

live.description: Live WAL execution state, if the invocation is still in flight.

recent_events.description: Most recent events for this invocation (newest first).

state_schema.title: InvocationDetailView

view.summary: An agent invocation: the fold of its lifecycle events.

view.description: Get answers with the roster row plus every invocation the worker owns; List answers with the roster rows alone. Neither derives a heartbeat age — the fold stays wall-clock-free, so a reader that wants an age computes it from `last_heartbeat_ms`.

filter_schema.description:
List selection for the Worker view — the typed, schema'd filter
(never a query language). `fq workers list` used to pull the whole
roster and sieve it in the client; the selection now travels with
the request and the view applies it to its index.
filter_schema.title: WorkerListFilter

index_schema.description: One worker in the roster: the Worker view's **index** row (`worker.list`).

in_flight_count.description:
Invocations this worker currently owns in a non-terminal state
(`in_flight` or `ambiguous`). Filled by [`Views::workers`] /
[`Views::worker`]; the bare `From<WorkerRow>` leaves it 0.

index_schema.title: WorkerView

key_schema.description: Get identity for the Worker view.

state_schema.description:
One worker plus the invocations it currently owns: the Worker
view's **state**, what `worker.get` answers with. `worker` is
nested rather than serde-flattened, and stays that way — the
nesting is `fq workers show --json`'s committed shape.

owned.description: Every ownership row for this worker (any status), newest first.

state_schema.title: WorkerDetailView

view.summary: A worker: the fold of its registration, heartbeats and ownership.

view.description: The answer is what this daemon would run right now — the registry `fq reload` swaps, not the definitions on the caller's disk. Get answers with one definition in full, including its system prompt. List answers with one row per definition file the registry knows: the agents it loaded, in id order, then the files it rejected, because a definition that failed to parse is the row an operator most needs to see and has no agent id to be listed under.

filter_schema.description:
List selection for the Agent view. Empty, and declared anyway: a
registry is a directory of definitions the daemon holds entirely in
memory, so there is no narrowing worth a wire contract yet, and the
declaration is where a future one would appear.
filter_schema.title: AgentListFilter

AgentSummaryView.description:
One agent definition in the daemon's live registry — the summary
row behind the dashboard's agents list and the Agent view's loaded
index row.

path.description:
The definition file this agent was loaded from. On the summary
as well as the detail because "which file is this?" is the
question a listing gets asked next, and answering it from the
index costs one string per row instead of one Get per agent.

prompt_bytes.description:
Size of the system prompt, so the list hints at definition
weight without shipping every prompt on every refresh.

trigger.description: The NATS trigger suffix the agent listens on, if any.

index_schema.description:
One row of the Agent view's index (`agent.list`): a definition file
the daemon read, and what became of it.

A registry snapshot is not only its agents. A file that failed to
parse is usually the most operationally interesting thing in the
directory — the agent someone expects to be running and is not —
and it has no agent id to be listed under, so it rides the index as
its own kind of row. Dropping it would make the listing lie by
omission, and there is nowhere else on today's surface to put it.

oneOf.description:
A definition the registry rejected, rendered exactly as the
daemon reports it — the message names the file.

index_schema.title: AgentEntryView

key_schema.description: Get identity for the Agent view.
key_schema.title: AgentViewKey

state_schema.description:
One agent definition in full — the Agent view's state (`agent.get`)
and the dashboard's agent detail page. Sourced from the daemon's
registry handle, so `fq reload` is reflected without a restart.

path.description: The definition file the agent was loaded from.

state_schema.title: AgentDetailView

view.summary: An agent definition, as the daemon's live registry holds it.

atom.description: Event-log-backed: `seq` is the stream sequence — the same cursor receipts, `min_seq` gates and `turn` sequences speak. List answers with the most recent `limit` matching events in sequence order, bounded by the tip observed at entry; Stream long-polls via next_batch from a sequence, and `from_seq = u64::MAX` seeks the tail without consuming anything. Resuming at a cursor loses nothing: the log is durable and the consumer is positional.

filter_schema.description:
List/Stream selection for Events — the typed, schema'd filter.

Never a query language, and deliberately never a bus subject: a
subject pattern is a coordinate of the infrastructure the edge maps
(D8), so the selection travels in domain terms and the daemon
decides which subjects answer it. It carries exactly the narrowing
`fq events query` offers, which is the same narrowing a tail wants.

agent.description: One agent's events. Absent reads the whole log.

event_type.description:
One event type, as the payload names itself (`llm_response`,
`tool_call`, `system_startup`, …). An unrecognised value
matches nothing rather than failing: event types are values,
and a newer daemon has types this binary has never heard of.

limit.description: Cap on one List page — the most recent N matching events.

since.description: Only events at or after this RFC3339 instant.

filter_schema.title: EventFilter

key_schema.description: Get identity for an Event: its event-log sequence.
key_schema.title: EventKey

state_schema.description:
One recorded event, addressed by its event-log sequence — the
universal cursor (P5): the same number that cursors `event.stream`,
feeds `min_seq` gates, and rides in a command receipt's `AtomRef`.

The Event atom's state is the event itself, unabridged. It is the
substrate every other resource folds from, so an atom that dropped
the payload would not be the fact; the projection's `events` table
is an *index* over these, not the atom.

event.description:
The event exactly as published.

Declared to the surface as an opaque object rather than a
reflected schema: an event already names its own payload
contract in `envelope.schema_id` (`factor-q/llm_response@1`),
which is the versioned reference a reader resolves, and
reflecting the whole payload tree here would need schemars'
chrono and uuid integrations — a wider change than this atom.

state_schema.title: EventState

atom.summary: One recorded event: the substrate every other resource folds from.

command.description: Returns a receipt naming the drop event's sequence — feed it to a gated read for read-your-writes. Refused on an invocation this daemon is actively driving unless `live` is set, which halts it at its next step boundary (in-flight tools finish) before the drop.

input_schema.description: The typed input of `invocation.drop` on the wire.

live.description:
Halt the invocation first if this daemon is actively driving
it. Without it, live work is refused outright — the kill
switch is opt-in, never implied (#107). Defaults false, which
is also what every peer that predates the field sends.

input_schema.title: DropCommandInput

command.summary: Drop an invocation: archive it as failed and release its owner.

atom.description: Event-log-backed: `seq` is the stream sequence — the same cursor receipts and min_seq gates speak. Stream long-polls via next_batch; from_seq = u64::MAX seeks the tail.

filter_schema.description:
List/Stream selection for Turns — full payloads by default; an
`abbreviate` option waits for a consumer that wants it (P11).
filter_schema.title: TurnFilter

key_schema.description: Get identity for a Turn: its event-log sequence.
key_schema.title: TurnKey

TurnAction.description: What happened: the turn's content, full payload by default.

oneOf.description:
The invocation's opening prompt: the system prompt the agent
was configured with and the user message its trigger became.
Folded from the opening `llm.request` — see
[`TurnFold::apply`]. First in the enum because it is first in
the conversation.

parameters.description:
Joined from the initiating call when it is in the fold's
window; `null` for a lone turn fetched by key.

state_schema.description:
One turn, addressed by its event-log sequence — the universal
cursor (P5): the same number that cursors `turn.stream`, feeds
`min_seq` gates, and appears in command receipts.

action.description: The action itself — the fact this atom records.

initiating_turn.description:
For a tool-result turn: the sequence of the assistant turn
whose call it answers — tracing in log coordinates. Absent
when the initiating turn predates the stream window, and on
turns no other turn initiated (assistant turns, the prompt).

round.description:
The Round grouping key: one Round is an assistant action plus
the tool results it initiated (the model-turn count
`max_iterations` gates). 0 on the opening prompt, which
precedes every Round, and on turns derived from events
predating the field.

state_schema.title: TurnState

atom.summary: One action within a Round: an assistant output or a tool result.
